33. A parallel plate capacitor is filled equally (half) with two dielectrics of dielectric constant $\varepsilon_{1}$ and $\varepsilon_{2}$, as shown in figures. The distance between the plates is d and area of each plate is A. If capacitance in first configuration and second configuration are $\mathrm{C}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ respectively, then $\frac{\mathrm{C}_{1}}{\mathrm{C}_{2}}$ is :
(1) $\frac{\varepsilon_{1} \varepsilon_{2}^{2}}{\left(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}\right)^{2}}$
(2) $\frac{4 \varepsilon_{1} \varepsilon_{2}}{\left(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}\right)^{2}}$
(3) $\frac{\varepsilon_{1} \varepsilon_{2}}{\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}}$
(4) $\frac{\varepsilon_{0}\left(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}\right)}{2}$

Ans. (2)
Sol.

Area of plate is A.
then
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_{2} \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d} / 2}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_{2} \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}} \\
\mathrm{C}^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_{1} \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d} / 2}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_{1} \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}
\end{array}$$

Let $\mathrm{C}_{0}=\frac{\varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{C}=2 \varepsilon_{2} \mathrm{C}_{0} \\
\mathrm{C}^{\prime}=2 \varepsilon_{1} \mathrm{C}_{0}
\end{array}$$

C \& C' are in series
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{C}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{CC}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{C}^{\prime}}=\frac{4 \varepsilon_{2} \varepsilon_{1} \mathrm{C}_{0}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{C}_{0}\left(\varepsilon_{2}+\varepsilon_{1}\right)} \\
=\frac{2 \varepsilon_{2} \varepsilon_{1} \mathrm{C}_{0}}{\left(\varepsilon_{2}+\varepsilon_{1}\right)}
\end{array}$$

Here $\mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_{1} \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{~A}}{2 \mathrm{~d}}=\frac{\varepsilon_{1} \mathrm{C}_{0}}{2}$
$$C^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_{2} C_{0}}{2}$$

C \& C' are inparallel
$$\mathrm{C}_{2}=\mathrm{C}^{\prime}+\mathrm{C}=\left(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}\right) \frac{\mathrm{C}_{0}}{2}$$

Thus $\frac{\mathrm{C}_{1}}{\mathrm{C}_{2}}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_{2} \varepsilon_{1} \mathrm{C}_{0}}{\left(\varepsilon_{2}+\varepsilon_{1}\right)} \times \frac{2}{\left(\varepsilon_{1}+\varepsilon_{2}\right) \mathrm{C}_{0}}$
$$=\frac{4 \varepsilon_{2} \varepsilon_{1}}{\left(\varepsilon_{2}+\varepsilon_{1}\right)^{2}}$$

46. Three identical spheres of mass $m$, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of length a. When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time $\mathrm{T}=4$ seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length 2a and also the masses of the spheres are made 2 m , then they will collide after $\_\_\_\_$ seconds.

Ans. (8)
Sol. $\mathrm{T} \propto \mathrm{m}^{\mathrm{x}} \mathrm{G}^{\mathrm{y}} \mathrm{a}^{\mathrm{z}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
T \propto M^{x}\left[M^{-1} L^{3} T^{-2}\right]^{y}[L]^{z} \\
T \propto M^{x-y} L^{3 y+z} T^{-2 y} \\
x-y=0 \Rightarrow x=y \\
-2 y=1 \Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{2}, x=-\frac{1}{2} \\
\Rightarrow 3 y+z=0 \\
z=-3 y=\frac{3}{2}
\end{array}$$

Hence
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{T} \propto \mathrm{~m}^{-1 / 2} \mathrm{G}^{-1 / 2} \mathrm{a}^{3 / 2} \\
\mathrm{~T} \propto\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}^{3}}{\mathrm{~m}}\right)^{1 / 2} \\
\mathrm{~T}=4 \times\left(\frac{2^{3}}{2}\right)^{1 / 2}=8 \mathrm{~s}
\end{array}$$
